newsitem.title: FRANCE: Second French boy hit by Zaire envoy's car dies.
newsitem.headline: Second French boy hit by Zaire envoy's car dies.

text.p: A second French boy hit by a car driven by Zaire's ambassador to France died on Saturday as demands mounted that the envoy be brought to justice or ordered out of the country.

The mayor of Menton and the local Gaullist parliamentarian both demanded that the government expel Ambassador Ramazani Baya if Zairean President Mobutu Sese Seko refused to lift his diplomatic immunity so he could be tried for the accident.
Ronald Lehartel, 12, had been in a coma in hospital since Wednesday, when he and a friend were hit by Baya's hired car on a pedestrian crossing.
Hospital sources said he died just after some 4,000 people marched through the town in a silent but angry tribute to his friend Raphael Lenoir, 13, who had been killed instantly.
Mayor Jean-Claude Guibal led the mourners, carrying white carnations, to the seafront raod where the accident occurred.
"We are very angry. (The envoy) is a man like any other and he deserves to be put on trial," said Guillaume, a friend of the two boys.
Guibal has asked Mobutu, who is in France, and French Foreign Minister Herve de Charette to waive Baya's immunity.
Parliamentarian Xavier Beck said he had asked de Charette to order the envoy out of the country unless he was required to stay on for an inquest into the accident.
Police have said Baya was speeding. A breathalyser test was negative, showing he was under the permitted drinking limit.
Foreign Ministry spokesman Yves Doutriaux said it was possible to declare a diplomat persona non grata, but he had no information at the moment that this could happen in Baya's case.
Baya had travelled to Menton to visit Mobutu, convalescing in nearby Roquebrune Cap Martin from cancer surgery in August.
Doutriaux said the families of the dead boys would be received on Tuesday by an aide to de Charette.

Demands for Ambassador Ramazani Baya to be brought to trial or ordered out of the country had been mounting after the car he was driving hit two boys on a pedestrian crossing in the Riviera resort of Menton last Wednesday.
One of the boys, Raphael Lenoir, 13, was killed instantly. The other, 12-year-old Ronald Lehartel, died on Saturday.

The ministry spokesman said the recall of the envoy was the usual diplomatic sanction in such cases. As long as he was in France, he was covered by diplomatic immunity and could not be brought to trial, he said.
Baya had travelled to Menton to visit Zairean President Mobutu Sese Seko, recovering in nearby Roquebrune Cap Martin from cancer surgery in August.
